title: Dataflow and Apache Beam: the same pipeline in batch and in stream

videos.script: Quitanda's order events arrive two ways. Every night a file of the whole day lands in a bucket. And all day long, each event is published to Pub/Sub the moment it happens. {{two}} The question asked of both is the same. How many orders did each neighbourhood place, and for how much? Writing that program twice is how two answers start to disagree. {{twice}} Apache Beam lets you write it once. A pipeline is a chain of steps over a collection, and the collection may have an end, or it may not. {{beam}} Dataflow is Google's service that runs a Beam pipeline on workers it starts for you. It is not the language. It is one runner among several. {{runner}} You will run the pipeline here, with Beam's DirectRunner, over a file and then over the Pub/Sub emulator. Only the two ends change, and the totals come out to the cent. {{same}} You will also see the one line a stream cannot do without, a window. {{window}} Then Dataflow itself, from Google's documentation, and its bill: a stream that never stops costs more than a night that does. {{bill}}
